newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt police kill Islamist militant in south.
newsitem.headline: Egypt police kill Islamist militant in south.

text.p: Egyptian police shot dead a suspected Islamist militant in an exchange of fire in the southern countryside on Friday, security sources said.

They said the militant, 26-year-old teacher Hamada Ismail Abdeldaim, had opened fire at police searching for him in fields near the village of Kafr Abdelkhaleq in Minya province about 160 km (100 miles) south of Cairo.
Police found a revolver and large quantities of ammunition next to his body, they added.
Police shot dead two other members of the militant Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) in the same area on Tuesday.
Abdeldaim was suspected on robbing banks in the provinces of Beni Suef and Giza to the north to finance the activities of the Gama'a, the largest group fighting the Egyptian government.
Police are hunting for a prominent Gama's member, Ahmed el-Basqalouni, who they believe was with Abdeldaim at the time of the shooting, the sources added.
The Gama'a has been fighting a low-scale guerilla war since 1992 to overthrow the government and set up a strict Islamic state. The police have contained its activities to Egypt's southern provinces.
Almost 1,000 people have been killed and scores wounded in the four years of political violence.
